The ESP32's WiFi — Connect the board to a network, check its Status, Scan for networks, make it an Access Point of its own, and Disconnect. What runs over it (HTTP, MQTT…) are components of their own.

credentials.name: wifi
credentials.description: A WiFi network to join — its name and password (2.4 GHz; the ESP32 doesn't do 5 GHz).

fields.name: ssid
fields.description: The network's name, as phones show it.

actions.description: Joins the board to a WiFi network — goes on (Out) once it has an address, Fallback when the password is wrong, the network isn't there, or it took longer than Timeout. Already on that network: on at once. The connection stays up while the flow keeps running — a session that ends (Run ▶, Debug, a once-mode Play) drops it.

configurations.description: The WiFi network to join — one of your credentials (its name and password), or a new one.
How long it tries before giving up, in ms — 1000 to 60000. The flow waits meanwhile.
The name the board shows in the router's device list — empty keeps the default (espressif).

outputSchema.name: ip
outputSchema.description: The board's address on the network, as text — empty when not connected.

outputSchema.name: ssid
outputSchema.description: The network it's on, as text.

outputSchema.name: rssi
outputSchema.description: The signal, in dBm — -30 strong, -70 fair, -90 barely there; 0 when not connected.

outputSchema.name: mac
outputSchema.description: The board's MAC address, as text — aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.

outputSchema.name: reason
outputSchema.description: Why it went Fallback, as text — wrong_password, no_network, failed, timeout, or no_credential (the network's credential isn't on the board: run the workflow again); empty once connected.

actions.description: Leaves the network, stops the board's Access Point, or both — the radio goes quiet for what's stopped.

configurations.description: What to stop — the connection to a network (Station), the board's own network (Access Point), or both.

actions.description: Branches on whether the board is on a network — Connected or Disconnected — with its address and signal, and how its Access Point is doing.

outputSchema.name: ip
outputSchema.description: The board's address on the network, as text — empty when not connected.

outputSchema.name: ssid
outputSchema.description: The network it's on, as text.

outputSchema.name: rssi
outputSchema.description: The signal, in dBm — -30 strong, -70 fair, -90 barely there; 0 when not connected.

outputSchema.name: signal
outputSchema.description: The signal as a percentage — 0 to 100.

outputSchema.name: ap_active
outputSchema.description: Whether the board's Access Point is on.

outputSchema.name: ap_clients
outputSchema.description: Devices joined to the board's Access Point.

actions.description: Lists the WiFi networks around, strongest first — an empty list when there's none (or the radio couldn't scan). Takes a couple of seconds.

outputSchema.name: networks
outputSchema.description: The networks it saw (the 10 strongest), strongest first, each with its ssid, rssi (dBm) and channel — bind it to a List variable or a list config.

actions.description: Makes the board a WiFi network of its own, for phones and other boards to join — goes on (Out) with its address (usually 192.168.4.1), or Fallback. Works alongside Connect. It stays up while the flow keeps running — a session that ends (Run ▶, Debug, a once-mode Play) turns it off.

configurations.description: The network's name, as others will see it.
8 characters or more (WPA2) — empty for an open network anyone can join.
The WiFi channel, 1 to 13 — another one if the air is crowded. With Connect on too, the board follows the network's channel.
How many devices may join at once — 1 to 10.

outputSchema.name: ip
outputSchema.description: The board's address on its own network, as text — usually 192.168.4.1.

Calls web APIs from the board — Request a URL (GET, POST…) with headers, a body and an auth token; the whole answer lands in a file the next actions read (Read JSON, the Filesystem component), and Pick takes one value out of its JSON right away. And serves them: Request Trigger runs a branch when a request comes in (a webhook), Respond answers it. Needs a network: WiFi's Connect before it.

credentials.name: http_header
credentials.description: A header sent with each request — an API key or a bearer token, kept out of the workflow.

fields.name: header
fields.description: The header's name — empty sends Authorization.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The header's value — "Bearer <token>", an API key…

triggers.description: Runs its branch when a request comes in on Port for Method under Path — a webhook, a page's button, another board. Answer it with Respond; a branch that doesn't answers 200. A path outside it gets 404, another method 405, a request without Auth's header 401. Needs WiFi (Connect on Start).

configurations.description: The base path it answers under — /api takes /api and everything below it (/api/led/on), read in subpath and segments; / takes every path. Two triggers on one port: the longer base path wins. The query (?a=1) doesn't count.
Which requests run it — Any, or only one method.
The port the board listens on — 80 is plain http://<board ip>/.
One value from the body's JSON, by its path — sensor.temp, items.0; empty picks nothing. Published as `value`.
An HTTP Header Auth credential the request must carry (that header, that value) — else 401. Empty lets anyone in.
A file of your own for the body — /data/last.json; it stays. Empty, it goes to a temporary file (one per trigger), cleared when a session starts.

outputSchema.name: method
outputSchema.description: The request's method — GET, POST…

outputSchema.name: path
outputSchema.description: The path it came for, without the query.

outputSchema.name: subpath
outputSchema.description: What came after the base path — /led/on for /api/led/on on /api; empty for the base itself.

outputSchema.name: segments
outputSchema.description: The subpath's parts, in order — ["led", "on"]; route on them with a Switch (segments[0]).

outputSchema.name: query
outputSchema.description: The query's fields as an object — ?led=on&level=3 is { "led": "on", "level": "3" }.

outputSchema.name: value
outputSchema.description: What Pick found in the body — a number, true/false, text, or a list/object as JSON; empty when nothing was picked.

outputSchema.name: file
outputSchema.description: The file holding the body — bind it to Read JSON or Filesystem's Read; empty when there was none.

outputSchema.name: size
outputSchema.description: How many bytes the body had.

outputSchema.name: client
outputSchema.description: The address it came from — 192.168.0.12.

outputSchema.name: error
outputSchema.description: What Pick missed, or why the body couldn't be saved; empty when all went well.

actions.description: Calls a URL — goes on (Out) on a 2xx answer, Fallback when there's no network, it took longer than Timeout, or the server answered 4xx/5xx (`error` says which). The board waits for the answer meanwhile.

configurations.description: What the request does — GET reads, POST sends, PUT/PATCH change, DELETE removes.
The address to call — https:// or http:// (without one, http://).
What POST, PUT and PATCH send — JSON, form fields or text. GET, HEAD and DELETE send none.
One value from the JSON answer, by its path — main.temp, weather.0.description (a number steps into a list); empty picks nothing. Published as `value`.
An HTTP Header Auth credential — the API key or token sent as a header. Empty sends none.
Headers to send — a name and a value each.
What the Body is — Auto takes JSON when it starts with { or [, text otherwise. A Content-Type in Headers wins.
A file of your own for the answer — /data/weather.json, its folders made; it stays. Empty, it goes to a temporary file, cleared when a session starts.
How long it waits for the server, in ms — 1000 to 60000.

outputSchema.name: status
outputSchema.description: The HTTP status — 200 OK, 404 not found, 500 server error…; 0 when no answer came.

outputSchema.name: value
outputSchema.description: What Pick found — a number, true/false, text, or a list/object as JSON; empty when nothing was picked.

outputSchema.name: file
outputSchema.description: The file holding the whole answer, as text — bind it to Read JSON, Filesystem's Read, or open() it in a Code binding; empty for HEAD or when it failed.

outputSchema.name: size
outputSchema.description: How many bytes the answer had.

outputSchema.name: error
outputSchema.description: Why it went Fallback, or what Pick missed — no_network, dns, timeout, refused, unreachable, http_404…, "pick: no field temp"; empty when all went well.

actions.description: One value from a JSON file on the board — a Request's `file` (bind it), or any other. Fallback when the file isn't there, isn't JSON, or has nothing at Pick.

configurations.description: The file to read — bind a Request's `file`, or a path like /data/response.json.
The value's path — main.temp, weather.0.description; empty takes the whole file (if it fits).

outputSchema.name: value
outputSchema.description: What Pick found — a number, true/false, text, or a list/object as JSON.

outputSchema.name: error
outputSchema.description: Why it's Fallback — no_file, not_json, no field temp, value_too_large; empty otherwise.

actions.description: Answers the request its Request Trigger's branch runs for — Status and a Body (or a File). Fallback when there's none to answer: not in a Request Trigger's branch, or it was answered already.

configurations.description: The HTTP status — 200 OK, 201 created, 400 bad request, 404 not found…
What it answers — text, or bind a list/object (sent as JSON).
What the Body is — Auto takes JSON for a list/object or text starting with { or [, plain text otherwise.
A file on the board to answer with instead of Body — /www/index.html. Empty sends Body.

outputSchema.name: error
outputSchema.description: Why it went Fallback — no_request, no_file; empty otherwise.

Directly reads or drives a single digital pin on the board.  Use this when no more specific component (Servo, etc) fits what you're wiring up.

actions.description: Sets the pin as output and drives it to the given digital value.

configurations.description: Board pin this GPIO instance controls.
Value of GPIO send.
configurations.label: HIGH

outputSchema.name: value
outputSchema.description: The digital value that was written (0 = LOW, 1 = HIGH).

actions.description: Sets the pin as input and reads its current digital value.

configurations.description: Board pin this GPIO instance controls.

outputSchema.name: value
outputSchema.description: The digital value read from the pin (0 = LOW, 1 = HIGH).

triggers.description: Runs its branch when a pin changes — a button pressed, a sensor going high.

configurations.description: The pin to watch.
Which change fires it.
The board's internal resistor — Up for a button wired to ground.
Changes closer than this to the last one are ignored (a button bounces), in ms.

outputSchema.name: level
outputSchema.description: The pin right after the change.

outputSchema.name: at
outputSchema.description: When it changed — the board's clock, in ms.
